messages:
linda.ae: Quick heads-up — Acme Health procurement wants to buy via AWS Marketplace with a 12-month committed spend. They have two must-haves: invoices (monthly, net-30) sent to Acme Holdings (different legal entity), and the private offer must reflect the committed discount exactly so their SAML procurement automation can match line items. Can Deal Desk + Legal confirm feasibility?
eli.dealdesk: Possible but not turnkey. We can issue an AWS Private Offer to set a custom price for the SKU to reflect the commit. AWS will still invoice, but we can add metadata and the PO number to help mapping. Legal will need to approve net-30 on the PO language — marketplace commerce often defaults to AWS terms.
neha.f: Procurement also insists on a single PO referencing the commitment and wants the monthly AWS invoice to include that PO number and the invoice entity = Acme Holdings. Can we guarantee a single invoice to Holdings if the usage comes from different Acme subsidiaries?
jonathan.c: Technical constraints: AWS marketplace invoices are issued by region/account; splitting usage across their subsidiaries will produce multiple invoices in many cases. If they require one invoice to Holdings despite multiple usage accounts, AWS may need to set a consolidated billing arrangement on their side. We can't force AWS to merge separate account invoices into one from our end.
sam.eng: For the POC we're running risk controls. They plan ~80k tokens/day for 30 days on hosted. For production commit we can include token caps and alerts to limit overage risk while marketplace billing catches up. I'll share sample quota rules.
eli.dealdesk: Actionable path: 1) AE (Linda) confirms commit amount and start date; 2) Deal Desk drafts Private Offer with custom per-SKU pricing that encodes the committed rate; 3) Legal reviews net-30 and DPA; 4) AR prepares mapping guidance linking AWS invoice IDs to our internal order_id so revenue ops can reconcile. Note: if they need split legal entities to be invoiced separately, we may need two private offers or a single master contract + invoicing solution from their side.
neha.f: Accounting note: even with Private Offer, the invoice origin is AWS. For our revenue recognition we need line-level mapping. Please ensure the private offer includes an order_reference tag we can use. AR, can you prepare a short mapping template?
ar.team: Yep — we'll draft an "AWS invoice mapping" spreadsheet template showing fields: AWS Invoice ID, Marketplace Order ID, SKU, quantity, gross, discount. We need the Private Offer ID to finalize.
legal-bot: Legal checklist: 1) DPA signature required; 2) confirm SOC/ISO artifacts provided; 3) approve special net-30 term for private offer. Please attach the Private Offer draft before signature.
procurement-bot: FYI: file a `mp-private-offer` ticket and tag with `procurement-sync`. Include PO sample and entity data.
linda.ae: Customer says they prefer a single invoice to Holdings. I'll ask whether they can centralize billing into Holdings (i.e., master payer account) temporarily. If they cannot, I'll ask if Holdings can accept a single invoice and manage internal chargebacks.
eli.dealdesk: If they cannot centralize, escalate to Partner Ops. We can model two Private Offers (US + EU) to match legal entities, but that increases operational overhead. Also note commit size thresholds for private offer discounts — need to confirm $/month.
jonathan.c: Additional technical gotcha: if they want usage-based SKUs (inference tokens) and embedding SKUs combined into a single line for procurement automation, Private Offer pricing may need to standardize on a bundled SKU or we provide a mapping doc.
neha.f: I'll gather the procurement automation rules (PO parser fields) and share. That will guide whether they need a single condensed line or multiple lines per SKU.
sam.eng: Sharing sample alert config now: `threshold: 70% of monthly commit -> email + slack @linda.ae`; sample gauge and quota commands included. This will let POC stay within budget.
linda.ae: Great. Next steps: I will confirm whether Acme can centralize billing, send commit amount (they're proposing $30k/mo), start date 2026-04-01, and list SKUs to include (inference + embeddings). I'll upload their PO example to the ticket.
eli.dealdesk: Once we have commit amount & SKUs, Deal Desk will draft the Private Offer and pricing worksheet and add order_reference tags. Legal will review net-30/DPA. AR to provide mapping template.
neha.f: Adding: procurement asked if we can invoice Holdings net-30 even though AWS invoices. Legal please confirm if we can route invoice instructions in the Private Offer.
legal-bot: We can request invoice instructions in the Private Offer metadata but cannot change AWS billing terms. We'll need AWS Partner Ops approval to guarantee net-30 to the buyer.
linda.ae: Thanks everyone. I'll update thread once I hear back from procurement. If they refuse centralization, I'll open a Partner Ops escalation.
eli.dealdesk: Noted. Tagging `deal-desk` and `partner-ops` for follow-up.
procurement-bot: Ticket created: `mp-private-offer-1776123456` — please attach draft PO and SOW.
